question.leadin: The man who assassinated this president bought an ivory-handled revolver for it because he thought it would look better in a museum.
question.text: Name this president who was shot by Charles Guiteau, a man who was bitter about not receiving a lucrative government job.
question.clue: This man defeated Winfield Scott Hancock to become president, and the Pendleton Civil Service Act was passed after his death.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about a famous American businessman who first became wealthy running a steamboat company.
swap.text: This man, nicknamed "commodore," was awarded a Congressional Gold Medal for the donation of his namesake steamship to the Union Navy.
swap.clue: During the California Gold Rush, this person created the Accessory Transit Company to bring passengers from the East Coast to San Francisco via Nicaragua.

question.text: This Scottish-American philanthropist, a founder of U.S. Steel, unsuccessfully offered to donate $20 million to purchase Filipino independence and counter American imperialism.
question.clue: His works include Round the World and Triumphant Democracy.

swap.text: The Teller Amendment, the U.S. helps to put down the Boxer Rebellion, and the Treaty of Paris ends the Spanish-American War.
swap.clue: This president won an election in which the "Cross of Gold" speech was given by William Jennings Bryan.

question.leadin: This man proclaimed, "you shall not crucify mankind on a cross of gold!" in a speech advocating for free silver.
question.text: Name this Democrat who was nominated for president on the Populist party ticket in the 1896 presidential election.
question.clue: He was cross-examined by Clarence Darrow during the Scopes Trial.

swap.leadin: A correspondence that hurt this man's presidential campaign ended with the incriminating phrase, "Please kindly burn this letter."
swap.text: Name this politician whose failed 1876 presidential campaign was hurt by the Mulligan letters. Eight years later, this man also lost out after Samuel Burchard gave a speech attacking "rum, Romanism, and rebellion."
swap.clue: Samuel Burchard hurt this man's presidential bid after claiming that the other party represented "Rum, Romanism, and Rebellion".

question.text: Bryan's presidential campaign was backed by this third party, which crusaded against banks and railroads on behalf of poor farmers.
question.clue: A vice-presidential candidate for this party was a champion of Rural Free Delivery named Thomas E. Watson.

swap.text: This man was Cleveland's opponent in the 1884 election. The "Mulligan Letters," which showed the scandalous business deals of this "plumed knight" in the railroad industry, repeatedly torpedoed his electoral hopes.
swap.clue: Bonds for the Little Rock and Fort Smith Railroad were the subject of this man's correspondence in the Mulligan Letters.

question.text: This Oglala Sioux fought a war with George Crook and aided Sitting Bull at Little Bighorn before he was killed at Fort Robinson.
question.clue: He teamed with the Hunkpapa Sioux in fighting the invasion of the Black Hills.

swap.text: After fighting against the Mexican government, he led a revolt on the San Carlos reservation against George Crook and surrendered to dishonest terms at Skeleton Canyon.
swap.clue: The operation that killed Osama bin Laden, Neptune Spear, was originally named for him.

question.leadin: Identify the following people connected with a certain strike.
question.text: The strike got ugly when the National Guard was called out under this general, who would later distinguish himself by leading the invasion of Puerto Rico in the Spanish-American War and capturing Geronimo.
question.clue: His other notable success was shared with Oliver Otis Howard and saw its climax at Bear Paw ravine.

swap.text: Dee Brown, who participated in the occupation of Alcatraz, wrote a history of the American West titled Bury My Heart at this location. Over 300 Lakota Sioux were killed in a 1890 massacre at this South Dakota location.
swap.answerHtml: Wounded Knee [or Bury My Heart at Wounded Knee]
swap.clue: The Big Foot Memorial Riders end their path at this place, remembering an event that began due to Black Coyote's deafness.

question.text: The National Equal Rights Party in 1872 nominated this first woman to run for president, even though she did not meet the constitutional age requirement. Frederick Douglass was unknowingly put on a ticket with this woman.
question.clue: (+) Although he never acknowledged the decision, Frederick Douglass was selected by this person to be their running mate on the Equal Rights Party ticket during the 1872 election.

swap.leadin: This book increased sympathy for poor immigrants by arguing that the squalor in which they lived was more a result of social forces than of personal immorality.
swap.text: Name this 1892 Jacob Riis (reese) book, which used photographs to illustrate the awful conditions in the overcrowded tenements of New York's slums.
swap.clue: This book contains a model colored map dividing its subject city into various ethnicities, and notes that the law defines its subject as "occupied by three or more families, living independently and doing their cooking on the premises."

question.leadin: In a case concerning these businesses, a New Orleans Benevolent Association sued the monopolistic company Crescent City, a corporation established by the Louisiana legislature.
question.text: Name these businesses that named a series of cases ruling that the Privileges and Immunities Clause protected only federal citizens.
question.answerHtml: slaughterhouses [accept meatpacking factories or meat processing factories; prompt on factories]
question.clue: In a case named for these places, Associate Justice Samuel Miller ruled that the Privileges and Immunities Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment applied only to federal citizenship and not the states.

swap.leadin: This man was introduced to anarchism through the Sila Club.
swap.text: Name this Polish-American anarchist who carried out an assassination at the Pan-American Exposition in 1901.
swap.clue: Hanna's fears were confirmed in September 1901 when this Polish anarchist fatally shot McKinley, leading to Roosevelt's assumption of the presidency

question.text: The Weather Bureau lost credence with the American public after failing to foresee this 1900 disaster that killed around eight thousand people and devastated a city known as the "Wall Street of the Southwest."
question.answerHtml: Galveston Hurricane [or Galveston Flood; or 1900 Galveston Hurricane; prompt on Great Storm of 1900]
question.clue: This 1900 natural disaster, a Category 4 storm that killed between six and twelve thousand people and is still the deadliest single-day event in US history.

swap.leadin: This politician was endlessly mocked by opponents for his statement "the tariff question is a local question" and accused an opponent of penning the Morey Letter.
swap.text: Name this good friend of Ulysses S. Grant who gained the nomination of the Democratic Party over Thomas Bayard in the 1880 presidential election. He commanded the II Corps during the Overland Campaign.
swap.clue: This general's counterattack at the Battle of Williamsburg made George McClellan call him "superb."

question.leadin: A 2015 biography by Edward O'Donnell titled [this man] and the Crisis of Inequality casts him as a social reformer whose ideas foreshadowed the Progressive Era and the New Deal.
question.text: Name this United Labor Party candidate who finished second in the hotly contested 1886 mayoral race in New York City, where he faced off against Tammany Hall's Abram Hewitt and Republican upstart Theodore Roosevelt.
question.clue: This man advocated a single tax on land as a solution for breaking the cycle of poverty in Progress and Poverty.

swap.text: This 1894 tariff, which slightly reduced rates from the McKinley tariff of 1890, had as one of its provisions a graduated income tax struck down by the Supreme Court in 1895.
swap.clue: The income tax provision that was struck down in Pollock had belonged to this piece of legislation.
